subject: ela
intro: When you come across a word you do not know, you have strategies to help you figure out its meaning. Two important strategies are: (1) using context clues — looking at the other words in the sentence for hints about what the unknown word means; and (2) using prefixes and suffixes — small word parts added to the beginning or end of a word that change or add to its meaning. Common prefixes include 'un-' (not) and 're-' (again). Common suffixes include '-ful' (full of) and '-less' (without).

items.prompt:
Use context clues to figure out what the underlined word means.
'The puppy was so tiny that it fit in the palm of my hand.'
What does 'tiny' mean?

steps: Look at the other words in the sentence for clues.
Clue: 'it fit in the palm of my hand' — the palm of a hand is very small.
If something fits in the palm of your hand, it must be very small.
The context clue 'fit in the palm of my hand' tells us that 'tiny' means very small.
solution.answer: 'Tiny' means very small. The context clue is 'fit in the palm of my hand,' which tells us the puppy was very small.

items.prompt:
Use context clues to figure out what the underlined word means.
'The children were very noisy during lunch — they were shouting and laughing loudly.'
What does 'noisy' mean?

steps: Look for clue words in the rest of the sentence.
Clue: 'shouting and laughing loudly' — these are loud actions.
The sentence gives examples of what being 'noisy' looks like: shouting and laughing loudly.
These examples help us understand that 'noisy' means making a lot of loud sounds.
solution.answer: 'Noisy' means making a lot of loud sounds. The context clues are 'shouting and laughing loudly.'

items.prompt:
Use the prefix 'un-' to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'The lid was stuck, so the jar was unopened.'
What does 'unopened' mean?

steps: Break the word into parts: 'un-' + 'opened.'
The prefix 'un-' means NOT.
So 'unopened' means NOT opened.
The context confirms this: the lid was stuck, so the jar was not opened.
solution.answer: 'Unopened' means not opened. The prefix 'un-' means not, so 'un' + 'opened' = not opened.

items.prompt:
Use the suffix '-ful' to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'She was careful not to spill her juice.'
What does 'careful' mean?

steps: Break the word into parts: 'care' + '-ful.'
The suffix '-ful' means full of.
So 'careful' means full of care — paying close attention so something bad does not happen.
The context confirms: she paid close attention so she would not spill her juice.
solution.answer: 'Careful' means full of care, or paying close attention. The suffix '-ful' means full of, so 'care' + '-ful' = full of care.

items.prompt:
Use the prefix 're-' to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'I made a mistake in my drawing, so I redrew it on a new piece of paper.'
What does 'redrew' mean?

steps: Break the word into parts: 're-' + 'drew.'
The prefix 're-' means again.
'Redrew' means drew again.
The context confirms: she made a mistake and then drew the picture again.
solution.answer: 'Redrew' means drew again. The prefix 're-' means again, so 're-' + 'drew' = drew again.

items.prompt:
Use context clues to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'The path through the forest was narrow — only one person could walk on it at a time.'
What does 'narrow' mean?
items.hint: Look for clues that tell you about the size or width of the path.

steps: Clue: 'only one person could walk on it at a time.'
If only one person fits, the path must not be very wide.
'Narrow' means not wide — thin or small in width.
solution.answer: 'Narrow' means not wide. The context clue 'only one person could walk on it at a time' tells us the path was thin.

items.prompt:
Use the suffix '-less' to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'Without his umbrella, he was helpless in the rain.'
What does 'helpless' mean?
items.hint: Break the word into parts: 'help' + '-less.' What does '-less' mean?

steps: Break the word: 'help' + '-less.'
The suffix '-less' means without.
'Helpless' means without help — unable to help yourself.
Context: without his umbrella, he had no way to protect himself from the rain.
solution.answer: 'Helpless' means without help or unable to help oneself. The suffix '-less' means without.

items.prompt:
Use context clues to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'The room was gloomy because all the curtains were closed and no light came in.'
What does 'gloomy' mean?
items.hint: Look at what is happening in the room. What would a room look and feel like with no light?

steps: Clue: 'curtains were closed and no light came in.'
A room with no light is dark and perhaps sad-feeling.
'Gloomy' means dark and dull, or sad and without cheer.
solution.answer: 'Gloomy' means dark and dull. The context clue 'no light came in' tells us the room was dark.

items.prompt:
Use the prefix 'un-' to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'The puppy was unhappy when its owner left for the day.'
What does 'unhappy' mean?
items.hint: Break the word: 'un-' + 'happy.' What does 'un-' mean?

steps: Break the word: 'un-' + 'happy.'
The prefix 'un-' means not.
'Unhappy' means not happy — sad.
solution.answer: 'Unhappy' means not happy, or sad. The prefix 'un-' means not.

items.prompt:
Use context clues to figure out the meaning of the underlined word.
'She was exhausted after running the race — she could barely keep her eyes open.'
What does 'exhausted' mean?
items.hint: Look for clues about how she was feeling or what her body was doing.

steps: Clue: 'could barely keep her eyes open.'
When someone can barely keep their eyes open, they are very, very tired.
'Exhausted' means extremely tired.
solution.answer: 'Exhausted' means very tired. The context clue 'could barely keep her eyes open' tells us she was extremely tired.
